full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J.: This petition for leave to appeal by the plaintiff-petitioner is from the judgment and decree dated 20.4.92 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division dismissing Second Appeal No. 336 of 1978 and thereby affirming the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court allowing Other Appeal No. 225 of 1977 dismissing Other Suit No. 180 of 1975 of the Court of Munsif, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong decreed by the learned Munsif by his judgment and decree dated 27.6.77. 

 4. The trial court decreed the suit on contest. Respondent No. 1 preferred Other Appeal No. 225 of 1976. The learned Additional District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 5.5.78 allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. The petitioner filed Second Appeal No. 336 of 1978 in the High Court Division. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division heard the appeal and by the impugned judgment and decree dismissed the appeal. 

 5. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that upon misreading of the report of local inspection and evidence on record the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erroneously held that the petitioner failed to prove his bonafide requirement. Next, he submits that although the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found that the notice under Section-106 of the Act was legally served upon respondent No. 1 he ought to have decreed the suit in view of the evidence of respondent No. 1 who stated that he is a tenant. 

 6. The learned Judge of the High Court Division held that the question of bonafide requirement is a question of fact and the lower appellate court being final court of fact rightly found on consideration of evidence that the plaintiff failed to prove bonafide requirement of the premises. The expression "bonafide requirement" con-notes an element of "must have" which the petitioner failed to prove. It has been consistently held by the Superior Courts that in order to evict a tenant the landlord must prove that he requires the premises bonafide meaning that his requirement is not a colourable pretext rather the need for the premises is a must short of which he will be deprived of his right to use his property. A finding on bonafide requirement is a finding of fact and the learned Single Judge rightly concurred with this finding of the lower appellate court. The impugned judgment and decree calls for no interference for the reasons stared above.
